description: An expander for Organism that filters the partials Organism is generating and can fill the gap with a plain wave; it goes immediately to the LEFT of the Organism it belongs to

params.text: Cycles the shape of the filter over the partials through lowpass, highpass, bandpass and notch
Chooses what the filtered-out partials are replaced with: a saw, a square, or nothing at all
Holds the first partial at the pitch set by Organism's V/Oct jack, exempt from whatever the current algorithm is doing to it
Sets how many partials the filter's slope is spread over, from one to about thirty-two
Sets which partial the filter is centred on, from the first to about the thirty-second
Sets a floor under the whole filter curve, so no partial is taken out completely
Scales the filter's depth, none at the far left and full at the far right
Thins the partials out by taking every nth one, -16 to 16; negative settings keep the ones a positive setting would remove
Sets the level of the envelope output below it, inverted anticlockwise of centre and silent at centre

inputs.text: Shifts the filter width, one doubling per two volts
Shifts the filter centre, one doubling per two volts
Shifts the filter floor, 10V covering the whole of that knob's travel
Shifts the filter depth, 10V covering the whole of that knob's travel; this jack also shifts the dither setting, which is a fault in Organism's expander code rather than something the panel says
Nothing reads this jack. Organism takes the dither modulation from the filter amount jack instead, so this one changes nothing whatever is patched into it

outputs.text: Organism's internal envelope, scaled by the knob beside it

notes: This module has no processing of its own. Every control on it is read by the Organism to its right, and with no Organism there nothing on it does anything

inputs.2:
±10V · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 1V.

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 1V.
